summary: A ROS Answers question (asked 2014-07-15 by user rnunziata) reports the error 'No valid hardware interface element found in joint' when loading the gazebo_ros_control simulation interface after moving from ROS Hydro to Ubuntu 14 / ROS Indigo. The asker shares the error log, Gazebo joint and plugin XML, a xacro transmission definition, and a YAML controller config for the rrbot example. An accepted answer by lockandfire (2014-07-20) explains that the Indigo version of the ros_control transmission parser requires a <hardwareInterface> tag inside both the <joint> and <actuator> sections, and that adding it to the joint fixes the error. Comments note a related ros_control bug report and a later fix in gazebo_ros_demos.
one_line: ROS Answers thread on fixing 'No valid hardware interface element found in joint' errors with gazebo_ros_control in ROS Indigo by adding hardwareInterface tags to transmission joints.
key_facts: The question 'No valid hardware interface element found in joint' was asked on 2014-07-15 by user rnunziata on ROS Answers.
The asker reported that the gazebo ros simulation interface worked in ROS Hydro but produced these errors after moving to Ubuntu 14 with ROS Indigo.
The error log reports 'No valid hardware interface element found in joint 'joint1'' and 'No valid hardware interface element found in joint 'joint2''.
The log also reports 'Failed to load joints for transmission 'tran1'' and 'Failed to load joints for transmission 'tran2''.
The controller initialization error reads: Could not find resource 'joint1' in 'hardware_interface::EffortJointInterface'.
The asker's Gazebo plugin was libgazebo_ros_control.so with robotNamespace /rrbot and robotSimType gazebo_ros_control/DefaultRobotHWSim.
The asker's xacro transmission tran2 used transmission_interface/SimpleTransmission with a hardwareInterface of EffortJointInterface inside the actuator section only.
The accepted answer by lockandfire was posted on 2014-07-20 and was described as the cause of the error in the Indigo version of ros_control transmission_interface transmission parser.
According to the answer, the parser checks for <hardwareinterface> tags in both the <joint> and <actuator> sections, while rrbot and other gazebo examples only had the tag in <actuator>.
The fix is to add <hardwareInterface>EffortJointInterface</hardwareInterface> inside the <joint name="joint1"> element of the transmission.
A commenter noted the change appears in the Indigo version of the ros_control package and suggested it is a ROS issue, and lockandfire filed an issue in the ros_control bug tracker (issue 177).
A comment dated 2014-08-02 marked the question as a duplicate of a gazebo answers thread and stated it was fixed by Kei Okada in the gazebo_ros_demos pull request 4.
The question had 9,457 views and was last updated on 2014-07-20 according to the page stats.
